LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is for the servo-nightly-bin package, a pre-built binary distribution of the Servo browser engine. The file follows standard AUR packaging practices: sources are fetched from the official GitHub repo (github.com/servo/servo-nightly-builds), checksums are provided and verified in the prepare() function, and the package() function performs only routine operations—installing desktop files, creating a shell wrapper that execs the binary, copying resources, and setting permissions. There are no network calls within the build script itself, no use of eval/base64/curl/wget in suspicious contexts, and no obfuscated or encoded commands. The heredoc creating the wrapper script (/dev/stdin with << END) is a common, safe pattern for generating shell scripts during packaging. All modifications (sed path substitution, chmod changes) serve the legitimate purpose of installing the application to the system. No evidence of data exfiltration, backdoors, credential theft, or execution of attacker-controlled code was found.

The sha256sums array contains three entries matching the three source files (the two binary archives and the LICENSE fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com), and the prepare() function verifies the tarball against its checksum—both ordinary and expected practices. The _datecode-derived URL and release-channel sourcing are consistent with how nightly builds are distributed. No genuinely malicious or dangerous behavior is present in this file.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR package: pre-built Servo binary, verified source</summary>
</security_assessment>
